samples.summary: New "empty color" predicate duplicates, and narrows, the existing canonical one in model/color.ts
samples.evidence: `clearEmptyStringKeys` tests `(style[key] as unknown) === ''` only. The repo already owns a canonical notion of "this stored color carries no color": `isEmptyStoredColor` in `packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:67`, used by `resolveStoredColor`, which accepts BOTH spellings the design doc says must count — the bare `''` (whitespace-trimmed) and the wrapped `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` a theme migration / PPTX import produces (docs-font-controls.md:266-267 "Both spellings of empty count"). The write-path helpers introduced here recognize only the bare, untrimmed `''`, so the read side and the write side of the same documented contract now disagree, and a second parallel definition of "empty color" exists in `model/types.ts` (a types module) rather than reusing/exporting the color module's predicate. Since a `StoredColor` object form is exactly what slides hands the docs stores, `{ backgroundColor: { kind: 'srgb', value: '' } }` still merges verbatim and reproduces the dead-value failure mode the change exists to prevent.

samples.summary: Design doc claims "every store write goes through one of them", but the content-PUT/backend tree serializer it names as a writer is not wired to the normalizers
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:274-292 states the `''`-means-clear rule is "a model-layer contract, enforced at the store boundary", explicitly lists "the content `PUT`" among the writers that motivate it, and tabulates the four wiring points — all four are in packages/docs and packages/frontend. The backend serializer that writes the same Yorkie tree, `serializeInlineStyle` in packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:84-86, does `if (typeof style.color === 'string') attrs.color = style.color;` and the same for `backgroundColor`, so a content PUT carrying `color: ''` still persists a dead empty attribute into the CRDT. `serializeCellStyle` there (line 155) likewise only skips falsy values instead of removing an existing attribute. Either the doc's "every store write" claim is overstated, or this writer is a missing wiring point. Same gap for the bulk write `YorkieDocStore.setDocument` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:763), which writes whole imported documents without normalization.

samples.summary: Clearable-key lists cover only `color`/`backgroundColor`, leaving the other color-valued style keys outside the stated contract
samples.evidence: The doc frames this as a general "`''` on a color key means clear" model-layer contract, but `CLEARABLE_COLOR_KEYS` omits `underlineColor` (and cell `borderTop/…` colors are nested inside border objects, so `normalizeCellStyleClears` cannot reach them). No picker writes those today, so this is a completeness/taste gap rather than a broken criterion, but the contract as documented is broader than the implementation.

samples.summary: Unrelated behavior change bundled into the fix: skipping `styleByPath` when the serialized attribute map is empty
samples.evidence: `if (Object.keys(attrs).length > 0) { tree.styleByPath(...) }` is an op-count optimization for clear-only cell edits, independent of the `''`-normalization the issue is about. Likewise the `CELL_STYLE_ATTR_KEYS` hoist + `satisfies` refactor (line ~253) is a cosmetic change riding along. Both are defensible but widen the diff beyond the stated scope, making the fix harder to review and revert in isolation.

samples.summary: Color-clearing semantics arguably belong in `model/color.ts`, not `model/types.ts`
samples.evidence: `model/color.ts` is already the home of stored-color semantics (`resolveStoredColor`, `isEmptyStoredColor`, `toRgbHexColor`, `storedColorsEqual`). Putting `normalizeStyleClears`/`normalizeCellStyleClears` in the types module splits one concept across two files; colocating them would also make the reuse of `isEmptyStoredColor` natural.

finding.summary: New "empty color" predicate duplicates, and narrows, the existing canonical one in model/color.ts
finding.evidence: `clearEmptyStringKeys` tests `(style[key] as unknown) === ''` only. The repo already owns a canonical notion of "this stored color carries no color": `isEmptyStoredColor` in `packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:67`, used by `resolveStoredColor`, which accepts BOTH spellings the design doc says must count — the bare `''` (whitespace-trimmed) and the wrapped `{ kind: 'srgb', value: '' }` a theme migration / PPTX import produces (docs-font-controls.md:266-267 "Both spellings of empty count"). verdict.reason: Verified in-repo: `clearEmptyStringKeys` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:271-283) recognizes only a bare, untrimmed `''`, while the package already owns a canonical "no color" predicate `isEmptyStoredColor` (packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:67-74) that trims and also accepts the wrapped `{kind:'srgb', value:''}` form, used by `resolveStoredColor` (color.ts:51). So a second, narrower definition of "empty color" now lives in the types module, and the documented read/write halves of the same convention disagree; `docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:265-267` states both spellings count within the very section (lines 244-311) that defines the store-boundary contract these helpers implement. The consequence is concrete: `storedColorsEqual` (color.ts:152-165) returns false for `({kind:'srgb',value:''}, undefined)`, so `inlineStylesEqual` (types.ts:468-469) permanently blocks re-merge — the dead-value symptom the change targets. types.ts:9 already imports from ./color.js, so reuse was readily available. Mitigating ambiguity exists (the task bullet at docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:30-32 and the write-path table at docs-font-controls.md:286-292 name only `''`; the object form on the write path may be hypothetical today), but that is not enough to name a refutation ground, so the finding stands as a reuse/spec-fit issue.

finding.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:274-292 states the `''`-means-clear rule is "a model-layer contract, enforced at the store boundary", explicitly lists "the content `PUT`" among the writers that motivate it, and tabulates the four wiring points — all four are in packages/docs and packages/frontend. verdict.reason: The unnormalized writers are real (backend docs-tree.ts:84-86,155 and YorkieDocStore.setDocument/writeFullDocument via serializeInlineStyle at yorkie-doc-store.ts:112-140), but they are explicitly out of the issue's scope and are already covered by the doc's stated approach, so this is not a spec-conformance/design-fit block. (1) The originating task docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:30-41 enumerates exactly the four wiring points that were implemented (types.ts helper, block-helpers.applyInlineStyle, YorkieDocStore.applyStyleInTree, Mem/Yorkie applyCellStyle), and its Non-goals at lines 52-56 explicitly exclude "Healing already-stored '' on document load (no migration pass)" — which is precisely what normalizing a whole-document PUT or setDocument would be. No acceptance criterion names the backend serializer. (2) The design doc does not silently overstate: docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:256-267 names the content PUT and PPTX/DOCX import as sources that "still hold the ''" and states the deliberate choice to tolerate them on read rather than migrate, repeated in the Out-of-scope paragraph at 308-311; line 249-251 pre-qualifies the table's sentence ("a store may still be *handed* one"). (3) The declared read-side guard genuinely exists: resolveStoredColor/isEmptyStoredColor in packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:47-74 collapse both '' and {kind:'srgb',value:''} to undefined at every paint-time read. What remains is that the table's phrase "every store write goes through one of them" is over-broad relative to the surrounding prose — a doc-wording precision nit, which under this lens is minor (the canonical subsystem doc exists, is updated, and is not a parallel file), not a failed acceptance criterion, duplicated module, or exceeded Non-Goal.

finding.summary: Table-cell background reset is an explicit Non-goal of the originating task, yet this delta implements it (memory + Yorkie `applyCellStyle`, `normalizeCellStyleClears`, new exports, tests) without updating the task's Non-goals list. `docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:44` still reads "Sheets / table-cell background reset (`applyTableCellStyle`) — different model", and the checklist (lines 30-39) names only `model/types.ts`, `store/block-helpers.ts` and `applyStyleInTree`. Either the scope reversal should be recorded in the task doc (Non-goal removed, steps added) or the cell path split into its own change; as it stands the design doc (`docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:246-259`, which now claims the contract covers "table-cell background") directly contradicts the task doc a reader would consult next.

verdict.reason: The finding's quoted evidence is not present in this tree. The task doc's Non-goals (docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:52-56) contains no table-cell / `applyTableCellStyle` entry — only #749, "Sheets background reset — different model", and no-migration. The checklist explicitly includes the cell work as a step (line 40-41: `normalizeCellStyleClears` + the boundary in `MemDocStore.applyCellStyle` and `YorkieDocStore.applyCellStyle`), and lines 43-50 record the scope reversal in prose with rationale ("The table-cell half started as a Non-goal and was pulled in… Sheets is still out — different model"), i.e. exactly the remedy the finding requests. The alleged contradiction with the design doc also does not hold: docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:286-297 documents both helpers and their store wiring, matching the task doc and the implementation (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:301-309, packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:289, packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2464-2467); both docs keep Sheets out of scope. The code exists, but the design-fit defect (undocumented scope reversal, doc-vs-doc contradiction) does not.
